title: RFK Jr. unveils sweeping federal initiative to find evidence of vaccine injuries
gist: HHS under RFK Jr. launched a four-part vaccine-injury initiative: an NIH clinic, paying doctors to file VAERS reports (possibly via a new CMS billing code), a VAERS overhaul contracted to SPN Solutions, and mandatory vaccine-injury fields in EHRs. Experts expect it to inflate perceived vaccine risk.

insights.claim: HHS opened an NIH clinic dedicated to patients with health problems after vaccination; it opened October 5 but was only announced later.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Signals institutionalization of vaccine-injury focus within federal research.

insights.claim: HHS proposes reimbursing doctors for VAERS reports, and the New York Times reported CMS may add a new billing code for it.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Financial incentives would likely raise VAERS report volumes, feeding litigation narratives.
insights.locator: HHS said the proposal to reimburse

insights.claim: The CDC awarded a nearly $1 million contract to Virginia-based SPN Solutions Inc. to make VAERS simpler and mobile-accessible.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Small federal health IT contracts flowing to new vendors.
insights.locator: In addition to providing a financial incentive

insights.claim: HHS will require electronic health records to include vaccine-injury information via the Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology
insights.so_what: New EHR data-standard requirements create compliance work for EHR vendors.

insights.claim: VAERS is an unvetted, open-submission early-warning dragnet, and the CDC finds most reports are not actually vaccine-related, yet anti-vaccine litigants cite it as evidence of danger.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Incentivized reporting could amplify spurious signals used in litigation.

insights.claim: Experts expect Kennedy's goal is not safety research but attacking vaccines by inflating risks and overemphasizing rare outcomes.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Policy risk for vaccine makers and public-health demand.

insights.claim: Protect Our Care's Brad Woodhouse warns paying doctors to report unproven harms invites higher insurance costs and waste, fraud and abuse.
insights.speaker: Brad Woodhouse
insights.so_what: Potential cost pressure on insurers and CMS.
insights.quote: Now Secretary Kennedy wants to bribe doctors to claim they see vaccine harm without proof, which is just asking for higher insurance costs
